modal_signal: may or may not update the entire set of bytes atomically
excerpt: An implementation may or may not update the entire set of bytes atomically.

modal_signal: may cause an illegal-instruction exception or may return a constant value
excerpt: Accessing an unimplemented counter may cause an illegal-instruction exception or may return a constant value.

modal_signal: an implementation may make VSXL be a read-only field
excerpt: In particular, an implementation may make VSXL be a read-only field whose value always ensures that VSXLEN=HSXLEN.

modal_signal: An implementation may have WFI always raise a virtual-instruction exception
excerpt: An implementation may have WFI always raise a virtual-instruction exception in VS-mode when VTW=1 (and `mstatus`.TW=0), even if there are pending globally-disabled interrupts when the instruction is executed.

modal_signal: is UNSPECIFIED and may be zero
excerpt: The number of bits implemented in `hgeip` and `hgeie` for guest external interrupts is UNSPECIFIED and may be zero. This number is known as _GEILEN_.

modal_signal: An implementation may make field UBE be a read-only copy
excerpt: An implementation may make field UBE be a read-only copy of `hstatus`.VSBE.

modal_signal: An implementation can choose to subset the delegatable traps
excerpt: An implementation can choose to subset the delegatable traps, with the supported delegatable bits found by writing one to every bit location, then reading back the value in `medeleg` or `mideleg` to see which bit positions hold a one.

modal_signal: the implementation may make FIOM read-only zero
excerpt: If S-mode is not supported, or if `satp`.MODE is read-only zero (always Bare), the implementation may make FIOM read-only zero.

modal_signal: Optionally, PMP checks may additionally apply to M-mode accesses
excerpt: Optionally, PMP checks may additionally apply to M-mode accesses, in which case the PMP registers themselves are locked, so that even M-mode software cannot change them until the hart is reset.

modal_signal: may contain additional CSRs
excerpt: an implementation may contain additional CSRs, accessible by some subset of the privilege levels using the CSR instructions described in Volume I.

modal_signal: implementations may convert an invalid address
excerpt: Prior to writing `mnepc`, implementations may convert an invalid address into some other invalid address that `mnepc` is capable of holding.

modal_signal: may safely set reserved and custom bits to zeros
excerpt: An implementation may safely set reserved and custom bits to zeros.

modal_signal: may implement `mseccfg` such that `[s,u]seed` is a read-only constant value
excerpt: Implementations may implement `mseccfg` such that `[s,u]seed` is a read-only constant value `0`.

modal_signal: may represent a subset
excerpt: `hpmevent__i__` may represent a subset of the state accessed by the `mhpmevent__i__` register.

modal_signal: may represent a subset
excerpt: Likewise, `cyclecfg` and `instretcfg` may represent a subset of the state accessed by the `mcyclecfg` and `minstretcfg` registers, respectively.

modal_signal: implementation-specific which DEPTH value(s) are supported
excerpt: It is implementation-specific which DEPTH value(s) are supported.

modal_signal: The optional MISP bit
excerpt: The optional MISP bit is set by the hardware when the recorded transfer is an instruction whose target or taken/not-taken direction was mispredicted by the branch predictor. MISP is read-only 0 when not implemented.

modal_signal: may optionally include a count of CPU cycles
excerpt: The `ctrdata` register may optionally include a count of CPU cycles elapsed since the prior CTR record.

modal_signal: may implement 0..4 exponent bits in CCE
excerpt: An implementation that supports cycle counting must implement CCV and all CCM bits, but may implement 0..4 exponent bits in CCE.

modal_signal: When the optional `__x__ctrctl`.RASEMU bit is implemented
excerpt: When the optional `__x__ctrctl`.RASEMU bit is implemented and set to 1, transfer recording behavior is altered to emulate the behavior of a return-address stack (RAS).

modal_signal: may or may not raise an illegal-instruction or virtual-instruction exception
excerpt: When a `stateen` CSR prevents access to state for a privilege mode, attempting to execute in that privilege mode an instruction that _implicitly_ updates the state without reading it may or may not raise an illegal-instruction or virtual-instruction exception.

modal_signal: it is implementation-defined whether bits SXLEN..XLEN of the destination register are unchanged or are overwritten
excerpt: When such a HINT is executed with XLEN < SXLEN and bits SXLEN..XLEN of the destination register not all equal to bit XLEN-1, it is implementation-defined whether bits SXLEN..XLEN of the destination register are unchanged or are overwritten with copies of bit XLEN-1.

modal_signal: An implementation may make UBE be a read-only field
excerpt: An implementation may make UBE be a read-only field that always specifies the same endianness as for S-mode.

modal_signal: may not be implemented
excerpt: Each standard interrupt type (SEI, STI, SSI, or LCOFI) may not be implemented, in which case the corresponding interrupt-pending and interrupt-enable bits are read-only zeros.

modal_signal: the implementation may make FIOM read-only zero
excerpt: If `satp`.MODE is read-only zero (always Bare), the implementation may make FIOM read-only zero.

modal_signal: optionally relaxes this alignment requirement
excerpt: The misaligned atomicity granule PMA, defined in Volume II of this manual, optionally relaxes this alignment requirement.

modal_signal: implementation-define short timeout
excerpt: `WRS.STO` (WRS-with-short-timeout) is provided that works like `WRS.NTO` but bounds the stall duration to an implementation-define short timeout such that the stall is terminated on the timeout if no other conditions have occurred to terminate the stall.

modal_signal: implementation-specific bounded time limit
excerpt: When the `TW` (Timeout Wait) bit in `mstatus` is set and `WRS.NTO` is executed in any privilege mode other than M mode, and it does not complete within an implementation-specific bounded time limit, the `WRS.NTO` instruction will cause an illegal-instruction exception.

modal_signal: implementation-specific bounded time limit
excerpt: When executing in VS or VU mode, if the `VTW` bit is set in `hstatus`, the `TW` bit in `mstatus` is clear, and the `WRS.NTO` does not complete within an implementation-specific bounded time limit, the `WRS.NTO` instruction will cause a virtual-instruction exception.

modal_signal: may define that accesses to certain CSRs are strongly ordered
excerpt: The hardware platform may define that accesses to certain CSRs are strongly ordered, as defined by the Memory-Ordering PMAs section in Volume II of this manual.

modal_signal: may be zero
excerpt: The duration of its effect must be bounded and may be zero.

modal_signal: can be implemented in software or hardware
excerpt: The tag checks themselves can be implemented in software or hardware.
